note: Error codes and HTTP statuses are proposals; milestone 03 fixes the registry. Row status names the decision record when one settles the behavior.

rules.text: No valid credential. Always 401 unauthenticated, whether or not the resource exists.

Authenticated, but the resource is missing, belongs to another workspace, or the principal has no membership in its workspace. 404 not_found with a body identical to a missing resource. Applies to nested references (site in an exploration state, site in a key grant, target of a transfer).
rules.basis: milestone 03 acceptance: guessed inaccessible ID; briefing: stale revisions rejected without disclosing inaccessible resources

rules.text: Explorations with visibility 'own' are visible only to their author. Workspace admins and owners get not_found.
Resource visible, capability missing. 403 forbidden. The required capability is a test annotation, not part of the response.
Operation needs the owner role on top of its capability (teams.delete, site transfer to a user).

Actor must outrank the target member and may not grant a role at or above their own, except that owners may make owners and change other owners' roles. Nobody changes their own role and the last owner cannot leave, so no team is left without an owner.
Any member may remove themselves from a team.
A key may call only the operations it holds. Checked before the resource is looked up. 403 operation_not_granted.
rules.status: briefing (Maintenance and security): "Scope keys to operations and sites."

rules.text: A key may touch only the sites it lists, even if the owner can read more. Other sites return not_found.
rules.status: briefing (Maintenance and security): "Scope keys to operations and sites."

rules.text: A key cannot hold more than its owner holds at creation or later, and can never hold reauthentication-gated, account, auth, 2FA, key, user or admin operations. Creating a key with an unseeable site returns not_found.
A revoked key returns the same 401 as an unknown key.

A share viewer reaches only the target site, operations, actions and recordings the share grants. A recordings grant includes listing and playing recordings that match the share's site, range and pinned filter. Everything else is not_found.
rules.status: briefing (Maintenance and security): "Reauthorize exports, recordings, shared explorations, and live subscriptions."

rules.text: Inside the granted operations, the request state may only narrow the share: no longer range, no dropped or OR-widened pinned filter, no measure, dimension or property outside the grants. The current and comparison ranges together must fit range_max_days. 403 share_scope_exceeded.
rules.basis: milestone 10: Sharing never broadens the underlying exploration or caller scope

rules.text: Unknown, revoked and expired share tokens return one response.

An idempotency key binds principal, operation and normalized argument fingerprint. Same triple returns the stored result; same key with different arguments is idempotency_conflict; a different principal's use of the key is a new key.
rules.status: briefing (Control transactions): "Bind each idempotency key to the principal, operation, and normalized argument fingerprint."

rules.text: A stored result is returned only after access is checked again with the current membership and capabilities.
rules.status: briefing (Control transactions): "Reauthorize access before returning a stored result after membership changes."

rules.text: Stored responses never contain a one-time secret. A replay returns the same key id with secret withheld.
rules.status: briefing (Control transactions): withholding policy required; response shape proposed

rules.text: Access and capability are checked before the expected revision. Only a caller allowed to write learns the current revision.
rules.status: briefing (Control transactions): "reject stale expected revisions without disclosing inaccessible resources."

rules.text: Subscriptions are reauthorized when membership, role, key or share state changes. Delivery stops with a terminal access_revoked event; reconnects with an old cursor get the same response as a missing resource.
rules.status: briefing (Control transactions and subscriptions): "Reauthorize delivery when permissions or sessions change."

rules.text: A correct password for an enrolled account yields second_factor_required and a partial token that is never a session. Wrong password and unknown user are the same response.

A user who must use 2FA but is not enrolled gets an enrollment-only session: twoFactor.begin, twoFactor.confirm, account.get, auth.logout. Everything else is 403 second_factor_enrollment_required. Confirming enrollment upgrades the same session. Existing sessions drop to enrollment-only at the next request when a requirement is switched on. API keys keep working.
Password change and auth.revokeSessions end the other sessions.
Initialization creates no account with a known password.
rules.status: briefing (Maintenance and security): "do not ship a known default password."

rules.text: Sensitive commands need a password check (and the second factor when enrolled) within the last 10 minutes of the login session: account.changePassword, twoFactor.disable, twoFactor.regenerateRecoveryCodes, twoFactor.begin and twoFactor.confirm while a factor is confirmed, apiKeys.create, members.updateRole to admin or owner, sites.delete, sites.reset, sites.transfer, teams.delete, users.delete, security.updatePolicy. Order: after the capability check, before the revision and idempotency checks. 403 reauthentication_required. Never grantable to a key.

users.delete is a durable job. It needs install.admin and reauthentication. Refused with 409 user_owns_resources while the user is the only owner of a workspace or owns personal sites, and with 409 last_install_admin for the last install admin. Effects are listed in scenario AX-S026.
Only committed results are stored under an idempotency key. A failed command stores nothing, so a retry with the same key runs again.
rules.status: adopted (decisions/0002-sessions-and-events.md, Request idempotency and batch IDs)

rules.text: An invitation code adds the signed-in person who redeems it to its team with its role, once. A person who is already a member gets the team and the code stays unused. Unknown, used, revoked and expired codes answer the same not_found.

default_session: Grid and targeted rows without a `session` field run in a login session that passed auth.reauthenticate in the last minute, so they test capability and visibility, not the 10 minute rule.
